Four short sessions fit the available 15-minute windows. Guidance fades from explicit steps to independent selection, application, and correction.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study one accurate model, explain it in your own words, repair any gap, then explain it again.

how: Say the rule in plain language from memory.
Compare your explanation with the model and fix missing parts.

activities.label: Product rule structure
activities.title: What the product rule says
activities.body: Read the model and watch the example structure.

activities.label: Say the rule aloud
activities.title: Explain the rule in your words
activities.body: Write the rule from memory in one or two sentences.
activities.correctAnswer: The derivative of a product is the derivative of the first factor times the second, plus the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: A complete answer states the two-term structure and the plus sign between the terms.

activities.label: Fix the missing part
activities.title: Repair the rule
activities.body: Revise your answer if any part was missing or out of order.
activities.misconceptionSummary: The rule is just the derivative of one factor times the other factor.
activities.correctAnswer: The product rule is (fg)' = f'g + fg', so both factors stay in the answer and each factor gets differentiated once.
activities.feedback: The repair is to include both terms, not just one derivative times one original factor.

activities.label: Explain it again
activities.title: Explain it again without copying
activities.body: Say the rule again in plain language.
activities.correctAnswer: When two functions are multiplied, the derivative is the first derivative times the second, plus the first times the second derivative.
activities.feedback: This shows the rule in plain language without relying on the exact formula wording.

activities.label: Recognize the rule
activities.title: Which expressions need it?
activities.body: Choose the option that needs the product rule.
choices: A single polynomial with no multiplication of functions
activities.feedback: The product rule applies when two functions are multiplied, not for a single polynomial, a constant, or a quotient.
